summary: Independent reproduction. (1) `python -m pytest -q`: 120 passed. (2) `python -m src.cli validate`: 0 problems, 0 open source conflicts. (3) `audit-verify` before 28 wrote anything: ledger OK (22 records). (4) Every table in reports/baseline/target_arithmetic.md (sections 1-4) was re-derived from config/model_config.yaml with standalone formulas that do not import src/economic_model, and compared cell by cell with the committed report: 50 of 50 row comparisons match exactly at the report's rounding. The platform's required_growth_table matches the standalone real-CAGR formula with zero absolute difference. Section 3 arrival years were re-derived by discrete annual compounding and match the report's ceil(log) formula. These are reproduced calculations on hypothetical assumption inputs (A-TGT-01..07), not estimates of Nepal's GDP. The arithmetic is VERIFIED; its application to Nepal is CONDITIONAL on those assumptions and UNVERIFIED until the base-year GDP and population are retrieved. Issues: the grid base year is a calendar-year label while Nepal's GDP is FY (01C ESC-03), and price/FX cases treat NPR depreciation independently of the INR peg (01C).

assumptions.text: Reproduction uses the report's own display rounding (2 dp for CAGR, 1 dp for I/Y) as the comparison precision.
Arrival year = first calendar-year label at which the discrete annual-compounding level reaches the target, matching math.ceil(base_year + years_to_target).

challenges.text: PF-4 (valuation-driven) and PF-5 (peg adjustment), as requested: PF-4 relies on sustained INR real appreciation against the USD plus a positive Nepal-India differential. Geopolitical stresses (S01 oil-price shock, S04 global recession, S10) typically bear on the INR and on regional risk premia, so PF-4 milestones should be reported as valuation-dependent and paired with an INR/USD stress, which no scenario provides yet (28C SC-05). A PF-5 peg step is a domestic policy decision; the platform should model its size only from historical parity changes (03A/20B) and must not imply any recommendation.

The target tables use calendar label 2025 as the base year while Nepal's GDP is fiscal-year. Please record the FY-to-label convention (01C ESC-03) in model_config before any verified base value replaces A-TGT-03.

uncertainty: Low for the arithmetic, which is deterministic and reproduced exactly. High for any Nepal-specific reading, because every input is a labelled assumption.
